content:
alice-support: heads up — customer svc-acme-77 reporting large billing delta after enabling continuous-batcher + kv-prefetch. Invoice INV-9921 shows 3.61M tokens billed but dashboard served_tokens ~1.20M. They attached a sample trace. Can eng/billing triage? :frowning:

ben-sre: On it. Can you confirm the deployment tag and whether caching prefetch is on the dedicated pool? Prefetch tends to generate background requests that look like requests to the metering pipeline.

alice-support: Deployment: cbatcher/v2.3 on dedicated-pool-west, kv_prefetch: true, prefetch_window_ms: 250, prefetch_group: default. Time window: 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z -> 2026-03-11T00:00:00Z. Attached minimal trace: (pasted below)

chun-ml: Quick read: we saw a pattern where continuous-batch warmup RPCs are issued to seed key prefixes. Metering runs at gateway boundary and charges tokens for warmup RPC input+generated prefix tokens, even if later the response is served from KV and not consumed by client. That would inflate billed tokens vs served.

dara-billing: Looking at reconciler: metered_tokens = 3,612,890, served_tokens metric = 1,198,540. Spike aligns with periods of high qps between 02:00-03:30 UTC where prefetch rate increased. Need exact trace to filter by request_id.

ops-bot: Created triage issue RW-INC-2026-118 in infra/inference. Repro checklist in issue.

ben-sre: Can you drop a small log snippet with request_id, meter_count, served_count? Also whether the request had header `X-Prefetch: true`.

alice-support: pasted snippet:

```
[2026-03-10T02:11:05.123Z] request_id=rid-7b1 meter_type=metered tokens_in=4096 tokens_out=1024 source=cbatcher prefetch=true service=svc-acme-77
[2026-03-10T02:11:05.456Z] request_id=rid-7b1 kvcache_lookup hit=true key_prefix=customer:svc-acme-77 result_tokens=1024 served_to_client=true
[2026-03-10T02:11:06.001Z] metering_event request_id=rid-7b1 billed_tokens=5120 pipeline_phase=gateway
```

chun-ml: That shows the pattern: gateway meters the initial prefetch request as full generation (4096 in) plus generated output tokens (1024) => billed 5120. Later kvcache returns hit and actual served_to_client is 1024. Our dashboard's served_tokens aggregates the 'served_to_client' metric; the billing pipeline uses 'gateway' metering which doesn't dedupe prefetch warmups.

dara-billing: So root cause is counting warmup prefetches at the gateway. Fix options: 1) mark prefetch requests with `X-Prefetch: true` and exclusion filter in metering; 2) dedupe metering by request_id when kvcache returned hit; 3) add separate metric for 'prefetch_billed_tokens' and surface in dashboard so customers can reconcile.

ben-sre: Short-term: let's add an exclusion rule in reconciler for requests with header `X-Prefetch` and create a billing credit for the spike window while we investigate. I'll also throttle prefetch concurrency by default for dedicated pools.

alice-support: Customer agrees to temporary credit, asked for timeline. ETA?

ben-sre: I'll patch reconciler filter and run a recount job — earliest by EOD (today). If recount reduces billed tokens, billing can issue credit. Assigning to dara-billing for credit approval.

dara-billing: Approving provisional credit if recount shows >20% discrepancy. Need a note for finance. :+1: 

chun-ml: Long-term we should change metering position: either dedupe on request_id after KV result, or carry 'is_prefetch' flag in proto so metering can ignore. Also add regression test in cbatcher e2e harness to prevent this from regressing.

ben-sre: Action items: (1) reconciler filter PR (2) recount job (3) cbatcher: tag prefetch header + e2e test (4) billing credit workflow. I'll open PRs and link here.

ops-bot: PR created: https://git.redwood/pr/infra/2791, recount job scheduled.

alice-support: Thanks — keeping customer updated. :tada:
